summary: Defines a YANG data model for configuring and managing devices that do IGMP and MLD snooping. Snooping lets a switch watch multicast group membership messages so it only forwards multicast traffic to ports that want it. The module follows the Network Management Datastore Architecture.

eli5.summary: A switch listens to who wants a show and sends it only to them instead of everyone.

subtitle: A standard YANG model for configuring and monitoring switches that snoop on IGMP and MLD multicast membership messages.

tldr.problem: Switches that snoop on multicast membership messages (IGMP and MLD) are configured in a different way by every vendor, and there is no common management schema for them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the YANG module ietf-igmp-mld-snooping. It adds separate IGMP and MLD snooping instances to the routing data model, attaches them to bridges and VLANs, and provides actions to clear group tables.
tldr.outcome: Operators and tools get one common way to configure snooping and read its state, using the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA). Optional features cover capabilities that not every device supports.

today: RFC 9166 is a Standards Track document (Proposed Standard, February 2022). It has not been obsoleted or updated, so it is the current definition of this YANG module.

sections.title: What the RFC Defines
sections.content:
RFC 9166 defines a YANG data model for managing devices that perform IGMP and MLD snooping, as described in RFC 4541. IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) and MLD (Multicast Listener Discovery) are the protocols hosts use to tell routers which multicast groups they want to receive.

The module conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342. The NMDA lets a client inspect the current operational values for configuration, so identical paths can be used to retrieve both the configured values and the operational values.
sections.eli5: Switches can peek at who asked to join a multicast group. This RFC is a common form for the settings of that peeking, like a standard remote control that works on every brand of TV.

sections.title: Design of the Data Model
sections.content:
An IGMP/MLD snooping switch analyzes IGMP/MLD packets and sets up forwarding tables for multicast traffic. Without snooping, multicast traffic is flooded in the broadcast domain. With snooping, it is forwarded based on the tables, which avoids wasting bandwidth.

The snooping switch does not need to run the IGMP or MLD protocols itself. Because snooping is independent of those protocols, the model does not augment, or even require, the IGMP/MLD data model of RFC 8652. The model covers IGMPv1, IGMPv2 and IGMPv3 for IGMP snooping, and MLDv1 and MLDv2 for MLD snooping.

IGMP snooping supports only IPv4 and MLD snooping only IPv6, so the RFC defines them as separate schema branches. That lets a device support either one or both independently, matches the style of RFC 8652, and allows small behavior differences to be modeled cleanly. The module does not cover L2VPN, which is left to a separate document.
sections.eli5: IPv4 and IPv6 get their own separate forms, because they are a bit different. A switch can fill in one form, the other, or both.

sections.title: Optional Features
sections.content:
The model represents the basic capabilities of snooping that any major existing implementation supports. Capabilities that not all devices have are declared as YANG features, so extensive use of features simplifies capability negotiation. Operational state parameters are generally not made features, because a device lacking one can usually derive a suitable value.

  • igmp-snooping and mld-snooping: support for each protocol.
  • fast-leave: do not send last member query messages to hosts.
  • static-l2-multicast-group and static-mrouter-interface: statically configured groups and multicast router interfaces.
  • action-clear-groups: the clear actions.
  • require-router-alert, lite-exclude-filter and explicit-tracking: router alert checking, the simplified EXCLUDE filter of RFC 5790, and per-host tracking of reports.
sections.eli5: Not every switch can do every trick. Each trick has a name tag, so a switch can say which ones it knows.

sections.title: Module Structure
sections.content:
The module ietf-igmp-mld-snooping augments the core routing model of RFC 8349 at /routing/control-plane-protocols/control-plane-protocol. It adds two containers: igmp-snooping-instance and mld-snooping-instance. Their structure is almost identical. The MLD instance uses IPv6 addresses and mld-version, while the IGMP instance uses IPv4 addresses and igmp-version.

Read-write nodes are configuration; read-only nodes are state. Each instance holds configuration such as enabled, send-query and querier-source, plus state such as entries-count, the dynamically learned bridge-mrouter-interface list, and a group list. Each group has sources and, with explicit tracking, a list of hosts with their filter mode.

Per-interface statistics count received and sent queries, reports, leave messages (done messages for MLD) and PIM hellos. Today the l2-service-type of an instance can only be set to bridge, and one instance corresponds to one bridge instance.

static-bridge-mrouter-interface is configured by an operator, while bridge-mrouter-interface is filled in dynamically by the snooping device.
sections.eli5: There is one binder for IPv4 and one for IPv6. Each has pages for settings you can change and pages that just show what the switch has seen.

sections.title: Timers and Defaults
sections.content:
Most configuration leaves mirror the IGMP/MLD query parameters of RFC 3376. The module sets these defaults:

  • query-interval: 125 seconds, the interval between General Queries sent by the Querier.
  • query-max-response-time: 100 deciseconds, the maximum time allowed before sending a responding report.
  • last-member-query-interval: 10 deciseconds, with a range of 10 to 10230. It can be tuned to modify leave latency.
  • robustness-variable: 2, with a range of 1 to 7, to tune for expected packet loss.
  • forwarding-table-type: ip, with mac as the alternative lookup mode.

enabled, send-query, explicit-tracking and require-router-alert all default to false. When require-router-alert is true, an IGMP or MLD packet without a router alert in the IP header is ignored. With fast-leave enabled, the software assumes that no more than one host is present on each VLAN port.
sections.eli5: The switch asks "anyone still want this show?" on a timer. The standard comes with sensible default timer settings, and you can change them.

sections.title: Bridges, VLANs and Clear Actions
sections.content:
An instance does nothing until it is attached to a bridge. The module augments /dot1q:bridges/dot1q:bridge with igmp-snooping-instance and mld-snooping-instance references, which enables snooping on the bridge. It also augments the VLAN node of the bridge component, which enables snooping in that specific VLAN. These nodes use the IEEE 802.1Qcp bridge model.

Two actions, clear-igmp-snooping-groups and clear-mld-snooping-groups, clear the group tables of an instance. Each takes a group and a source. If both source X and group Y are given, only source X of group Y in that instance is cleared.
sections.eli5: You plug a snooping instance into a bridge, or just into one VLAN. A clear button wipes the switch's list of who wants what.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is accessed through management protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF, which run over SSH and TLS respectively as the mandatory-to-implement secure transports. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) of RFC 8341 can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

The writable nodes under the snooping instances, including those under the bridge and VLAN, are sensitive. Unauthorized writes can cause network malfunctions and delivery of packets to inappropriate destinations. Read access also matters, because group, source and host information can expose multicast group memberships and, transitively, the association between a user and the content from a source.

The clear actions are sensitive too. If invoked without authorization, especially with a wildcard, the group tables are cleared and all multicast traffic is flooded in the broadcast domain. Devices using the module should also heed the security considerations of RFC 4541.
sections.eli5: Only trusted people should hold the remote control. Someone who can wipe the list or peek at it could mess up the show or learn who watches what.
